facts.text: The Crucible was a primordial convergence of all living things, described in item descriptions as the source from which all life in the Lands Between originally came.
In the age of the Crucible, life was not divided into species or hierarchies but existed in chaotic communion, with traits like tails, wings, and carapaces expressing freely.
An older tree called the Great Tree existed at the center of the Crucible age, predating the current Erdtree, referenced in items like the Root Resin and the Crucible Knight armor set.
Ancient dragons existed before the Golden Order and may have had their own prior cosmic order and god predating the Greater Will.
A distant cosmic presence called the Greater Will sent a daughter, Marika, and a golden being called the Elden Beast toward the Lands Between.
The current Erdtree grew around the Elden Ring, absorbing and subsuming the older Great Tree that existed before it.
The Golden Order reached an accommodation with some ancient dragons rather than conquering all of them outright, as evidenced by dragon communion rituals involving consuming dragon hearts.
An incantation description states that everything was originally in opposition to the tree, but through countless victories in war it became the embodiment of order.
Murals from the Golden Order's early era, called the Age of Plenty, depict the Erdtree standing straight and tall, unlike its leaning posture in the game's present.
Before the Erdtree, the horns of an Omen signified divinity, but after the Golden Order's establishment, Omens were seen as cursed beings without grace, having their horns cut off and being enslaved.
Traces of the Rune of Death spread through the Erdtree's root network, appearing as Death Root.
The spread of the Rune of Death created a new category of beings called 'those who live in death,' undead people who cannot properly return to the Erdtree.
Every demigod touched by a Great Rune's concentrated power was driven toward madness.
The Tarnished's journey leads through demigods, ruins, underground cities, and frozen mountaintops before reaching Leyndell, the royal capital.
The Erdtree in the game's present cannot be entered, its golden bark sealed over by thorns that no conventional weapon can break.
Sorcerers claim the Erdtree is withered while priests claim it is merely dormant awaiting a new Elden Lord.
The Realm of Shadow contains the Gate of Divinity, the same gate Marika used to become a god.
The game identifies at least half a dozen Outer Gods clearly, with hints of others whose names remain obscure.
The God of Scarlet Rot is an ancient deity that was defeated and sealed beneath the lakes, in what became the Lake of Rot.
The Formless Mother, also called the Mother of Truth, is the Outer God that Mohg worships, associated with burning blood, wounds, and brutal intimacy.
The Fell God is depicted as a malformed one-eyed deity with curled horns and braided red hair, associated with primordial fire preceding the Erdtree's golden warmth.
The Frenzied Flame is delivered through the Three Fingers, said to be a counterpart to the Greater Will's Two Fingers, once part of a single whole.
The Dark Moon, Ranni's chosen Outer God, is cold, silver, and distant, governing fate, stars, and the unknown, offering freedom rather than commandment.
The player character is called Tarnished, one who once had the grace of the Erdtree, lost it, was exiled, died, and is now called back by a new Grace to seek the Elden Lordship.
The ruins of Limgrave suggest a civilization that was once whole.
The Academy of Raya Lucaria represents a tradition of magical scholarship that persisted stubbornly even as the world fell apart.
The Mountaintops of the Giants reflect a genocide carried out in the name of order.
The Lands Between is ruled by Queen Marika the Eternal, and the Elden Ring is the source of the Erdtree.
Demigods are described as warped Lords who began as members of a royal and noble family, ruling their domains with power granted by shards of the Elden Ring.
Those blessed by the Elden Ring and Erdtree are marked by a golden aura visible in their eyes.
The Lands Between is divided into seven distinct areas: Limgrave, Caelid, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Mt. Gelmir, Mountaintops of the Giants, and underground river locations.
Each of the seven areas of the Lands Between is overseen by a Demigod.
If an Empyrean defies the will of the Two Fingers, their Shadow is fated to go mad and oppose them.
The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC takes players to the Realm of Shadow, a dark, death-filled counterpart of the Lands Between hidden beneath a shrouded cloud south of the Erdtree.
The Realm of Shadow features the Scadutree, a shadowy counterpart to the Erdtree.
The DLC's story centers on the ambitions of Miquella, Messmer, and St. Trina, and explores the history of the Hornsent faction.
The Nox were punished for a rebellion against the Greater Will, their cities forced underground as a form of exile.
The Fell God is the ancient fire deity of the giants that Marika and Godfrey went to war against in the early days of the Golden Order.
The ancient people of Mt. Gelmir worshipped a powerful serpent god, offering it sacrifices.
Marika directed Godfrey to wage war against the Fire Giants because their flame of ruin threatened the Erdtree.
Godfrey fought and made peace with some ancient dragons, and defeated the Storm Lord alone in single combat, an event still echoed in Stormveil Castle's architecture.
Godfrey led the campaign against the Fire Giants, the defining war of the early Golden Order, which nearly annihilated the giants entirely.

One Fire Giant was deliberately spared and chained at the Mountaintops of the Giants; since Marika could not extinguish the flame of ruin at the Forge of the Giants, she cursed it to guard the forge flame forever, intending its use for opening the Erdtree.
When Godfrey destroyed nearly all the giants, the Fell God lost most of its followers but did not die, and still lurks in the Mountaintops of the Giants.
Rennala's mastery of lunar magic allowed her to become head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and its Glintstone Knights, and to establish the Carian family as royalty.
After the Fire Giant war ended with no enemies remaining, Godfrey's spirit declined without purpose, so Marika stripped him and his warriors of their grace, making him the first Tarnished.
Godfrey's armies and kinfolk were stripped of grace and exiled, via the Long March across the Sea of Fog, to the Badlands, told to fight and die there away from the Lands Between.
Marika promised the exiled Tarnished that after death she would eventually return their grace and give them a chance to return and serve as Elden Lord.

The people of the eternal cities (referred to as the 'Dox people') were once the most advanced scholars of the Lands Between, studying stars and cosmic forces and building underground cities lit by artificial constellations.
Radagon's previous marriage to Renala, Queen of the Full Moon of the Carian royal family, was a political alliance between the Golden Order and the Carian sorcerers.
The Finger-Slayer Blade was made in Nokron by a people who had rebelled against the Greater Will and were punished by having their entire civilization buried underground.
As chieftain of the badlands, Hoarah Loux was a fierce warrior with strong bloodlust before being selected as Marika's consort.

Marika ordered Maliketh, the Black Blade, her Shadow and half-brother entrusted with the Rune of Death when the Golden Order was established, to lock away the Rune of Death, also called Destined Death.
Queen Marika's first consort was Godfrey, with whom she had three children: Godwyn the Golden and the Omen twins Morgott and Mohg.
Royal-blooded Omens, including Morgott and Mohg, were hidden from the world and shackled in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath Leyndell.

On behalf of the Greater Will, Marika and her followers waged wars to spread the Golden Order's influence, most notably against the Storm Lord, the fire giants and their god the One-Eyed God, and the Academy of Raya Lucaria and Carian royal family.
It is unclear which side instigated the wars against the Dragons and against the Godskin Apostles and their god, the Gloam-Eyed Queen.
During Godfrey's reign, gladiatorial combat in colosseums across the Lands Between was common as rituals honoring the Erdtree, a practice that ended when Radagon became Marika's consort.
Marika summoned Radagon back to the Erdtree capital to become her second Elden Lord consort, ending his marriage to Renala; together they had the twins Miquella and Malenia.
Kale's nomadic clan, the Great Caravan, was accused of heresy and buried alive underground, where they summoned the flame of frenzy.
Marika tasked Radagon with leading the Erdtree's armies in the war against Liurnia of the Lakes.
Godfrey's axe was broken in battle during the Long March, and after the journey he reverted to being a simple warrior while still carrying Serosh on his back.

Sword monuments in Liurnia suggest there were two Liurnian Wars; it was after the second, when Rennala met and fought Radagon, one of the Erdtree's champions, that they fell in love and reconciled, seeking absolution together at the Church of Vows using Celestial Dew, where they were married, uniting Leyndell and the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Radagon and Rennala had three children together: General Radahn, Praetor Rykard, and Lunar Princess Ranni.
Radagon gifted Rennala an Amber Egg and left her to rejoin Marika's side when Godfrey and his fellow Tarnished were exiled.
When Godfrey was exiled and Radagon returned to Marika's side, Rennala was devastated and grew weak, losing her charm over the Academy.
The Academy's scholars rebelled against the Carian royal family, with the Cuckoo Knights attacking Caria Manor and locking Rennala in the Grand Library.

On a night of wintry fog the Rune of Death was stolen, a fragment of it used in the Night of the Black Knives, and the demigods began to fall, starting with the death of Godwyn the Golden, the first demigod to die in the Lands Between's history.

Ranni the Witch rejected her fate of being controlled by the Two Fingers and masterminded the Night of the Black Knives, stealing a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and imbuing it in the Black Knife Assassins' blades.
On the Night of the Black Knives, assassins killed Godwyn the Golden and carved a death curse mark meant to fully erase both body and soul.

At the exact moment Godwyn died, Ranni took her own life at the top of an isolated tower in the Lands Between, which split the intended death curse mark into two half-circles instead of one complete circle.

Shabriri was the name of a man punished for slander by having his eyes gouged out, after which his eyes filled with the flame of frenzy; according to the Howl of Shabriri, this was the first instance of the maddening sickness of frenzy in the Lands Between.
One night, Rennala took her daughter Ranni out stargazing as she had done in her own childhood, which led to Ranni meeting her own moon, the Dark Moon.

Messmer was tasked with purging the tower-dwelling Hornsent, who are known as Omens in the Lands Between and represent an older religion predating Marika's rule; his forces decimated the Hornsent people.
Rykard met Tanith, a dancer in an unnamed foreign land, and brought her back to the Lands Between to be his consort.
One half of the curse mark was carved into Godwyn's flesh, and the other half was carried away by Ranni's discarded body.
The knife that killed Godwyn only carried a fragment of the Rune of Death, so it killed only his soul, leaving his body alive but soulless.
Ranni's body died but her soul survived because she had planned for this outcome in advance, needing to die in the flesh while preserving her soul in order to escape the Two Fingers' control.
Ranni transferred her soul into a small doll modeled after a mentor she had loved, the Snow Witch Renna, then vanished from the world's awareness.
Ranni, Marika's stepdaughter, used a piece of Marika's own system to murder Marika's firstborn son Godwyn.

When Mohg stood before the Formless Mother, an outer god similar to the Greater Will, his cursed blood caught fire and the deity chose him as her vessel due to his crucible-marked omen nature, granting him bloodflame incantations.
Godwyn's soulless body grew and festered within the underground roots beneath Leyndell, becoming the entity known as the Prince of Death.
Godwyn's death devastated Queen Marika, being the most devastating loss among the many kin killed that night, since he embodied everything she hoped the Golden Order could produce.
Rykard encountered the God-Devouring Serpent and offered himself and his Great Rune as sacrifices to gain immortality, allowing him to grow and devour people and gods for eternity.

Following Godwyn the Golden's death, Marika took the Elden Ring and shattered it, her final act of rebellion against the Greater Will, breaking the fundamental laws of reality and the order of the world, resulting in her imprisonment within the Erdtree and triggering the war between the demigods known as the Shattering.
The shards of the shattered Elden Ring flew outward and were claimed by Marika's demigod offspring, becoming their Great Runes, whose corrupting power triggered the Shattering.
Rykard's fall into greed and gluttony caused most of his followers to turn against him, with Tanith remaining a notable exception.
Radahn halted the stars specifically to prevent Ranni's planned Age of Stars from occurring, since her destiny required the stars to fall.
Malenia marched her army from the Haligtree south to fight Radahn in the Battle of Aeonia, the defining conflict of the Shattering.
Malenia's Cleanrot Knights, who accepted exposure to scarlet rot out of loyalty, fought Radahn's soldiers in one of the bloodiest battles in Lands Between history.

Malenia and Radahn were evenly matched in personal combat, as neither had ever lost a battle before, and their duel ended without a victor, demonstrating that no single faction in the Shattering could achieve decisive victory even when empowered by a Great Rune.
During the duel, Malenia's needle broke, though the game leaves ambiguous whether this happened by accident or by her own choice.
When Malenia's needle broke, the scarlet rot suppressed within her since birth exploded outward as the Scarlet Aeonia, a massive crimson flower as large as a small city.
The bloom of the Scarlet Aeonia transformed the region of Caelid into a permanent blood-red rotted wasteland.
After the battle, Malenia fell into a deep, dreamless coma.

Former Gelmir Knights sought out the great spear Serpent-Hunter, designed to kill the immortal God-Devouring Serpent, to stop Rykard, but were unsuccessful, as evidenced by corpses found holding the weapon in his boss room.
A Cleanrot Knight named Finlay carried Malenia's unconscious body alone back to the Haligtree, fighting off enemies the entire way.

After the Shattering ended without a decisive victor, the demigods retreated to their strongholds; Leyndell remained mostly intact but without a true Elden Lord, and the Shattering meant abandonment of the Lands Between by the Greater Will.
Miquella grew the Haligtree from a sapling, watering it with his own Empyrean blood hoping his growth would be reflected in the tree, but it never became a full Erdtree.

While Malenia was fighting Radahn, Mohg, Lord of Blood, kidnapped the sleeping Miquella from within the Haligtree and took him to his hidden palace underground, trying to rouse him with his accursed blood, but Miquella never woke despite Mohg's offerings and shared bedchambers.
Mohg wrapped Miquella in a cocoon of golden silk and fed him blood in a ritual meant to elevate Miquella to divine status.
Through symbolic death in Mohg's cocoon, Miquella broke free of the Erdtree's death-rebirth cycle and shed his flesh piece by piece on his path to the Gate of Divinity.
Malenia sleeps in the depths of Elphael, the branch of the Haligtree, waiting for Miquella to return.
Even during Malenia's sleep, the scarlet rot she carries continues to spread and corrupt the Haligtree, which Miquella intended as a pure sanctuary.
On a night of wintry fog, a group of unknown assassins struck across the Lands Between, killing many of Queen Marika's kin.
To prevent the Rune of Death from being stolen again, Maliketh bound his sword, imbued with the rune, within his own body and changed his name.
The Shattering was a devastating war between Queen Marika's demigod children, breaking the empire she had united into fragments.
After Malenia's Scarlet Aeonia bloomed in Caelid during the Shattering, Gowry dedicated his services to her, believing she would found a new Order of Rot.
General Radahn recruited Jerren into his army as a guest commander during the Shattering, before he could fulfill his promise to slay Sellen.
Mohg eventually escaped the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and established Mohgwyn Palace in a secluded part of the Siofra River.
Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring is portrayed as a deliberate act by a god who no longer believed in the system she built, not an accident or madness.
Despite being the same person, Marika and Radagon held different wills; when Marika shattered the Elden Ring, Radagon used the same hammer to try to repair it.
During the Shattering, when Leyndell was leaderless, Morgott secretly ruled the capital as the Unveiled Monarch, knowing it wouldn't accept an Omen as leader.
During the Second Defense of Leyndell, Morgott successfully defended the capital and the Erdtree from invading demigods.
Vyke took the Frenzied Flame into himself to save his finger maiden from being sacrificed to burn open the Erdtree.
Vyke became a Lord of Frenzy and lost his path to the throne, wandering into madness.
Radahn's loyal soldiers organized the Radahn Festival, inviting warriors worldwide to give their general an honorable death in battle rather than kill him for conquest.
Miquella later attempted to use the same Gate of Divinity at Anor Ilim to claim his own godhood, as depicted in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

When Radahn was defeated at the Radahn Festival, the stars he held moved and a fragment struck the earth, opening the previously inaccessible underground city of Nokron, which was exactly what Ranni needed for the next stage of her plan.
Ranni seeks the Finger-Slayer Blade, hidden in the underground city of Nokron, to pursue her plan involving the Dark Moon.
Ranni travels to the Moonlight Altar, a remote plateau guarded by a sleeping ancient dragon coiled around a cathedral of sorcery, to claim the Dark Moon Ring meant for her Elden Lord consort.
Ranni leaves the Dark Moon Ring for the Tarnished to retrieve and bring back to her, formally asking them to be her lord and consort.
Leda hints at a tumultuous past between the Hornsent and the tower folk, resulting from ancient conflicts instigated by Queen Marika's commands.
The Dragon Communion Priestess provides lore about Bayle and Placidusax, revealing the former dominion and decline of the Ancient Dragons.
The Fire Giants were one-eyed beings who worshipped a primitive fire god predating the Golden Order and tended a red flame of ruin capable of burning the Erdtree.
The Nox, also called the people of the eternal cities, were builders and scholars who constructed underground metropolises lit by artificial stars.
The Crucible Knights are ancient warriors who served under Godfrey but whose design and incantations point to a time before the Golden Order existed.
The Misbegotten were strong, winged beings who were later enslaved under the Golden Order.
The Omens were beings born bearing physical traits of the old Crucible, such as horns, which the Golden Order later declared signs of corruption.
Marika constructed the Golden Order, a system of divine law and metaphysics based on the runes composing the Elden Ring.
The Golden Order, established by Queen Marika when brought to the Lands Between by the Greater Will, is the most dominant faction in the land.
The Black Knife Assassins were an elite group of Numen women with mysterious ties to Marika, armed with death-imbued knives and wearing near-invisible cloaked armor.
Those who live in death were hunted by the Golden Order for existing in a state that violated its framework of mortality.
Rykard's Volcano Manor became a refuge for assassins and recusants who rejected the Golden Order and hunted tarnished.
The Greater Will effectively went silent after the Shattering, unable or unwilling to guide events.
Mohg recruited followers for the Mohgwyn Dynasty, offering deals to some like Bloody Finger Okina and kidnapping others like the War Surgeons.
After the Shattering and the Greater Will's departure, some Golden Order followers began questioning the Order's infallibility.
The Two Fingers are disembodied hands of the Greater Will that communicate through a sign language understood only by trained finger readers, and they select mortal Empyrean candidates for godhood.
Followers of the Frenzied Flame are scarred, one-eyed people whose eyes burn with yellow fire, believing the end of everything would be a mercy.
Tanith is now the Lady of the Volcano Manor, recruiting Tarnished willing to rise against the Greater Will and become recusants.
Recusants who prove themselves worthy at Volcano Manor are granted an audience with Rykard, where they are devoured by Rykard himself and become part of the Volcano Manor family.
Volcano Manor houses a group of Recusant Tarnished led by Praetor Rykard, seeking to rebel against the Erdtree.
Volcano Manor's notable members include Bernahl, Tanith, Patches, Praetor Rykard, and Rya.
The Mohgwyn Dynasty is led by Mohg, Lord of Blood, and like Volcano Manor its members invade other Tarnished and renounce the Greater Will, but bloodshed is their sole motive.
The beginnings of the Mohgwyn Dynasty can be found at Mohgwyn Palace, and its notable members include Mohg, White Mask Varre.
The Carian Royal Family faction's remaining members are Rennala, Ranni, and their trusted advisors after the Academy's scholars rebelled.
Serving the Carian royal family now means serving Ranni in her mission to usurp the Two Fingers and Greater Will, rebelling against her fate as an Empyrean.
Notable members of the Carian Royal Family faction include Blaidd, Preceptor Seluvis, Ranni the Witch, Rennala, and War Counsellor Iji.
Those Who Live in Death refers to the numerous undead in the Lands Between, whose existence defies the Golden Order and leads to their persecution.
Members sympathetic to Those Who Live in Death await the rise of their Lord, Godwyn, Prince of Death, the first of the dead demigods.
Fia is a notable member associated with Those Who Live in Death.
Notable Golden Order members include Brother Corhyn, D Hunter of the Dead, D's Twin Brother, Goldmask, Kenneth Haight, Radagon, and Queen Marika.
The Frenzied Flame is a covert faction led by the Three Fingers, who serve an unknown Outer God that rejects the Greater Will and blames it for the world's problems.
Frenzied Flame followers await a Lord of Chaos who will burn the world down to end its troubles.
Notable Frenzied Flame members include Hyetta, Nomadic Merchants, the Three Fingers, and Shabriri.
The Hornsent is both an individual character and the name of a race originating from the Realm of Shadow.
Marika was originally a Newman (Numen), a rare people from outside the Lands Between, chosen and brought to the Lands Between by the Greater Will to serve as their vassal.
Marika was chosen as an Empyrean candidate by the Two Fingers and became a god at the Gate of Divinity in Anor Ilim.
Godfrey was a chieftain from the Badlands, an extraordinarily powerful warrior consumed by a lust for battle.
Marika's first consort in the ritual of godhood was Hoarah Loux, a warrior chieftain from the Badlands, who would become known as Godfrey, the first Elden Lord.
Marika chose Hoarah Loux as her consort because he was the best warrior in the world, needed to conquer resisting peoples for the Golden Order.
Rennala was a young astrologer who, after a chance encounter with the Full Moon, learned its magic and became one of the most powerful glintstone sorcerers.
After being exiled, Godfrey reverted to being Hoarah Loux, wandering and fighting for the pure pleasure of combat while waiting for Marika's promise to be fulfilled.
The dragon Fortissax formed a genuine bond of friendship with Godwyn the Golden, Godfrey and Marika's noble, widely beloved firstborn son.
Radagon previously married Renala, Queen of the Full Moon, after defeating her sorcerers in battle and proposing peace through union.
Radagon and Renala had three children together: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni.
Godfrey and Marika's twin omen sons, Morgott and Mohg, were hidden and thrown into the sewers beneath Leyndell at birth because their crucible-like deformities were considered shameful.
The Tarnished is a being who once possessed the grace of the Erdtree, lost it, died, and endured a strange persistence that being Tarnished grants.
Upon becoming consort, Godfrey took Beast Regent Serosh upon his back to quell his bloodlust and become more fit to be a Lord.
Mohg is a son of Queen Marika and Godfrey, and unlike his twin Morgott, fully embraced his accursed Omen nature.
Because Marika and Radagon are the same being, Renala was in effect abandoned by the very god she had helped ascend, though she does not consciously realize this.
Because Marika and Radagon are a single god, their children Miquella and Malenia were described in-game as born of a single god and were cursed from birth.
Miquella was cursed with eternal youth, forever trapped in a child's body, unable to grow into the mature form required for godhood.
Malenia was born harboring the Scarlet Rot, marked by the God of Scarlet Rot from birth per the Remembrance of the Rot Goddess, a corruption that eventually consumed her eye, arm, and leg.
Messmer, son of Marika and brother to Miquella and Malenia, is cursed with the Abyssal Serpent inside him.

Ranni the Witch renounced her flesh and transferred her soul into a porcelain doll modeled after a mentor she loved, dying in the flesh on the Night of the Black Knives in order to preserve the freedom of her soul and set her plan in motion.

Radahn is a massive lion-armored general who studied gravitational magic in Sellia, a Caelid town known for sorcerers who studied stars and cosmic forces, partly so he could continue riding his small horse Leonard, whom he'd owned since childhood, without crushing it under his growing size.
Radahn used gravity magic to halt the movement of the stars, locking the constellations in place to prevent an unwanted destiny.
The Taker's Cameo item description implies Rykard believed Marika and her Order ruled by force, prompting him to swear himself to blasphemy and seek to overthrow them.
Miquella envisioned a world without discrimination that would welcome those rejected by the Golden Order, including albinaurics, the misbegotten, and omens.

Rykard became the Lord of Blasphemy, a ruthless justiciar and son of Rennala and Radagon who presides over Mt. Gelmir, merging with a great serpent god and turning Volcano Manor into a haven for rebels and assassins who reject the Greater Will's authority.
Morgott, though shunned and reviled in Leyndell his entire life, eventually escaped confinement and dedicated his life to protecting the city that had reviled him.
Godfrey served the Golden Order with absolute commitment and was exiled for having run out of wars to fight.
Miquella developed a theology of 'unalloyed gold,' a form of divine power independent of the Greater Will, and used it to grow the Haligtree as a sanctuary.
Malenia serves as Miquella's sworn protector and champion, and is said to have never lost a battle except her final one.
Mohg escaped his confinement but turned toward worship of an outer god called the Formless Mother, building a hidden palace of blood devotion around a wound in the earth.

Mohg believed he was a devoted caretaker enabling Miquella's ascension; because he is not an Empyrean and cannot ascend to godhood himself, he hoped to raise Miquella to full godhood and become his consort to claim the title of monarch.
Malenia gave everything for her brother's cause and is depicted as still waiting for him to return.
Morgott's dialogue suggests he attempted to claim the throne of Elden Lord but was warded off by the Erdtree.
Vyke, a tarnished, was according to item descriptions closer to becoming Elden Lord than anyone before the player character.
Nepheli's questline involves confronting the horror of Stormveil's population being experimented on and turned into shambling creatures by Godrick.
The Tarnished first encounters Morgott under the pseudonym Margit, blocking their path to challenge Godrick at Stormveil Castle.
Godrick the Grafted was a weak descendant of Godfrey's line who surgically attached the limbs of conquered warriors to his own body to compensate for his inadequacy.
Alexander travels toward the Radahn Festival out of genuine joy at the prospect of fighting alongside great warriors.

Melina's true goal, only understood at the end of the story, is to sacrifice herself as kindling to burn open the Erdtree so the Tarnished can enter it; at the Forge of the Giants she carries this out, stating she does not know what she will become but does not regret the choice.
Despite being abandoned by Marika, Messmer continues his mission and becomes a dominant figure in the Realm of Shadow.
Sir Ansbach is a former servant of Mohg who now follows Miquella in the Realm of Shadow.
At the end of his questline, Alexander requests to be defeated by the player so his absorbed essence can be carried forward.

Redmane Freyja was once deeply loyal to General Radahn, having fought alongside him in past battles, but became a devoted follower of Miquella after he healed a scarlet rot wound on her helmet, leaving a permanent scar she now views as her guiding compass.
Freyja urges the Tarnished to follow the footprints of Miquella, expressing readiness to fight again and a duty to understand and honor the vow Miquella made with Radahn.

Early in the DLC it is revealed these characters were united under Miquella's charm, and when he breaks a rune arc to free them, the group becomes divided and uncertain, revealing his manipulative side.
At Raya Lucaria Academy's Grand Library, Renala clutches an amber egg given to her by Radagon as a parting gift, believing it contains her beloved Radagon and refusing to accept his departure.
Miquella possesses a supernatural charm that compels affection from others, including demigods, which he has used deliberately to further his goals.
Miquella, cursed with eternal youth, seeks to achieve godhood by completing a ritual involving capturing Radahn's soul and placing it into Mohg's body.
Rykard was served by the Gelmir Knights, and the lava sorceries usable by the Tarnished were created by him, some derived from old Mt. Gelmir hexes.
Ranni was an Empyrean, a candidate to become the next god of the Lands Between under the Greater Will; although not born a demigod, she became eligible due to Radagon's unity with Marika.
Ranni wanted to escape the fate chosen for her by the Two Fingers and refused to continue Marika's cycle of divine control.
Ranni is introduced to the player in a tower in northern Liurnia, one of three towers belonging to her and her brothers, once her family's home before her father Radagon left to return to Marika.
Ranni appears as a young woman with pale blue skin and silver hair inhabiting a small doll body.
Ranni's retinue includes Blaidd, a half-man half-wolf sworn to serve her; Iji, an ancient blacksmith; and Sellen, a snow witch whose loyalty is complex.
Alexander the Iron Fist is a giant jar, a living vessel called a 'jarhead' containing the remains of great warriors absorbed into it.
Alexander is found stuck in the ground up to his shoulders, calling cheerfully for help, and wants to grow stronger by absorbing the remains of great warriors.
Nepheli Loux is the granddaughter of Gideon Ofnir, the all-knowing leader of the Round Table Hold faction.
Nepheli Loux is the adoptive daughter of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, who named her his heir even in exile.
Nepheli Loux is the adoptive daughter of Sir Gideon Ofnir, who took her in when she became Tarnished after losing grace.
Nepheli Loux loses faith in Sir Gideon Ofnir after learning he orchestrated the attack on the Village of the Albinaurics.
It is speculated that Nepheli Loux has ties to Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, based on sharing the surname Loux with Hoarah Loux and Kenneth Haight deeming her worthy to lead Limgrave.
Fia, the Deathbed Companion, resides in the Round Table Hold and offers an embrace that grants a buff and a debuff simultaneously.
Fia collects deathbeds, the moments of heroes' final rest, carrying them inside her body to eventually create the Prince of Death made possible by Godwyn's incomplete demise.

Melina walks beside the Tarnished as a guide, tending the Sites of Grace, and has no grace or permanent vessel of her own, appearing only through temporary forms; she serves as the Tarnished's Finger Maiden in exchange for being taken to the Erdtree and later the Mountaintops of the Giants.
Melina offers the Tarnished fragments of information and a kindness that seems genuine despite being largely unexplained.
Melina describes herself as someone born at the foot of the Erdtree who was given a purpose by her mother, whom she believes can be found there, leading to speculation that her mother is Marika.
Melina may be a child of Marika existing outside conventional demigod lineages, or a soul given form by the Erdtree, or a deliberate contingency created by Marika.
Melina appears at Sites of Grace as though existing at the margins of the world rather than at its center.
Melina can recall echoes of Queen Marika's past actions and words when spoken to at Sites of Grace.
Melina holds contempt for the Frenzied Flame and believes its lord is no true Lord.
If the Tarnished takes the Frenzied Flame before the event at the Forge of the Giants, Melina will leave and threaten to deliver Destined Death.
Goldmask, using the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, concluded that the flaws of the Golden Order come from the fact that gods are as flawed and fickle as the mortals they govern.
Fia is empathetic toward and devoted to the cause of Those Who Live in Death, considering herself their guardian.
Godwyn's incomplete death produced an entity called the Death Prince, combining Godwyn's lingering flesh presence with the rune of death.

The Dung Eater has committed atrocities against both the dead and the living and wants to spread his personal curse to all beings in the Lands Between and all future generations, so everyone is equally defiled, by gestating the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse.
Miquella's compassion was genuine, but his methods were controlling and manipulative in ways his good intentions do not fully excuse.
Fia held dying Tarnished in her arms out of compassion because she believed someone needed to.
Goldmask sat in silence at the edge of a great ruin, working out the nature of the universe without writing anything down, believing the right person would understand without words.
General Radahn is described as 'the conqueror of the stars' and Malenia the Severed as 'the Blade of Miquella'.
The White Masks at Mohgwyn Palace were abducted by Mohg, Lord of Blood, and turned into Bloody Fingers through a ritual involving his Omen blood.
Of the four White Masks encountered, only Varre was able to withstand and tame the accursed blood.
White Mask Varre remains loyal to the Mohgwyn Dynasty and tries to indoctrinate the Tarnished into it.
At the end of his questline, White Mask Varre, forsaken by Mohg, still calls out to him and blesses the Mohgwyn Dynasty as he dies.
Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is a samurai from the Land of Reeds who hunts down Bloody Fingers.
Yura's biggest target is Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, a Tarnished he holds in high regard.
Yura warns that those who partake in Dragon Communion eventually lose their humanity.
Some Bloody Fingers encountered by the Tarnished have been swayed by Mohg, the Lord of Blood.
Sorcerer Rogier was once a scholar seeking the truth behind the Night of the Black Knives.
Rogier's scholarly pursuits led him under Stormveil Castle, where he disturbed a corpse and became afflicted with Death.
Unlike D, who sees Those Who Live in Death as a threat to the Golden Order, Rogier is empathetic toward them.
Finishing Rogier's quest reveals insights about the Night of the Black Knives before he succumbs to his affliction.
Fia is a Tarnished Deathbed Companion driven from her home when awoken by the guidance of grace.
A Deathbed Companion receives warmth and life from champions and then lies with the remains of an exalted noble to revive them, a practice revered in Fia's homeland.
Fia's champions include Rogier and Lionel the Lionhearted, a knight who claims to be her father.

By combining Ranni's half of the Cursemark of Death from the Divine Tower of Liurnia with Godwyn's half from D, Fia implies Godwyn could be reborn as the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince through her role as his Deathbed Companion.
D, Hunter of the Dead is a devout follower of the Golden Order who hunts Those Who Live in Death, especially Tibia Mariners for their Deathroot.
D has a twin brother whose name is implied to be Darian.
D and his twin brother share the same soul and body, and cannot be conscious at the same time despite having separate bodies and minds.
D and his twin found comfort in the Golden Order, which was the one order that did not consider them cursed.
D states that Those Who Live in Death violate the principles of the Golden Order and must be exterminated.
D's twin brother is inferred to be named Devin based on D's voicelines.
D, Beholder of Death can be found slumbering in Siofra Aqueduct while D is alive, and grieving there if D is dead.
D's twin brother swears revenge on his brother's killer, whether it be Fia or the Tarnished, when given his brother's armor.
Gurranq, Beast Clergyman is a large beastman who hungers for Deathroot.
D was previously in charge of hunting and providing Deathroot to Gurranq before the Tarnished took over.
It is heavily implied that the Beast Clergyman found in Crumbling Farum Azula is Gurranq himself, and that Gurranq is Maliketh, the Black Blade.
Maliketh is Marika's Shadow, bestowed on her by the Greater Will as an Empyrean, similar to how Blaidd is Ranni's Shadow.
According to the Stone of Gurranq, Maliketh was a ferocious warrior whose name meant 'Death of the Demigods'.
Maliketh's Remembrance implies he was betrayed by Marika, though the details are unknown.
Roderika is a Tarnished driven away from her home across the sea, and her cloak implies she was once royalty.
Roderika met White Mask Varre, who gave her the same advice he gives the Tarnished: to seek Godrick and his Great Rune at Stormveil Castle.
The men escorting Roderika at Stormhill were taken and sacrificed for grafting, leaving her guilt-ridden for being too afraid to join them.
Roderika moves to the Roundtable Hold and is trained by Smithing Master Hewg to become a skillful spirit tuner.
Roderika stays behind with Hewg even as the Roundtable Hold burns, to repay his kindness.
Smithing Master Hewg is a misbegotten chained and imprisoned at the Roundtable Hold, tasked by Queen Marika with forging a weapon strong enough to kill a god.
Hewg believes the Tarnished will become Elden Lord, and states so before losing his memory completely.
Kenneth Haight is a member of Erdtree royalty and self-proclaimed rightful leader of Limgrave, owner of Fort Haight.
Kenneth Haight looks down on Godrick for his cowardly actions during the Shattering and for lacking proper lineage to rule.
After retaking Fort Haight, Kenneth Haight seeks an eligible candidate to rule Limgrave and eventually finds Nepheli Loux.
Gatekeeper Gostoc is the gatekeeper of Stormveil Castle who nonetheless informs the Tarnished of a safer side passage.
Gostoc secretly follows and steals a portion of the Tarnished's Golden Runes each time they are defeated in the castle.
Gostoc holds contempt for Godrick, having been mistreated by him, and longs for freedom from his duties.
When Nepheli Loux takes the throne, Gostoc is happy to return to his duties.
Boc the Seamster is a demi-human outcast who admires his late mother, a skilled seamstress.
Boc was expelled from the Coastal Cave and had his possessions stolen by other demi-humans.
After the Tarnished helps Boc reclaim his Sewing Needle and Tailoring Tools, he offers to tailor their armor.
The Tarnished can help Boc by giving him a Larval Tear to change his appearance or by telling him he is beautiful, and he is grateful either way.
Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order whose armor implies he once foretold an inauspicious prophecy.
Corhyn leaves the Roundtable Hold in search of Goldmask, a scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism.
Corhyn acts as Goldmask's scribe, translating his finger movements into written records.
Corhyn begins to question Goldmask's intentions after learning of his reservations toward the Golden Order.
Goldmask is a famed scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism who does not speak, communicating instead through rhythmic hand and finger movements.
Goldmask once lamented that hunters of Those Who Live in Death had become fanatics who hunted merely to have an evil to fight.
Gowry is a Kindred of Rot disguised as an old sage and was Millicent's caretaker as a child.
Gowry found Millicent and presumably her sisters as babies in the swamp of Aeonia and raised them hoping they would become scarlet valkyries under Malenia.
Gowry saw the most potential in Millicent among the sisters to follow Malenia's path.
At the end of Millicent's quest, Gowry asks the Tarnished to help Millicent's sisters attack her, believing betrayal will trigger her to 'bloom'.
Millicent is a daughter of Malenia, sharing her mother's red hair, missing arm from scarlet rot, and swordsmanship style.
Due to scarlet rot, Millicent does not remember her childhood with Gowry despite feeling familiarity at his shack.
After being cured with the Unalloyed Golden Needle, Millicent seeks out Malenia to help her resist the scarlet rot.
Millicent is ambushed by her sisters at Elphael before reaching Malenia.
If defended by the Tarnished, Millicent reveals she knows what Gowry hoped she would become, then removes the golden needle and succumbs to scarlet rot to remain herself.
Irina is the blind daughter of Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne.
Irina escaped Castle Morne with her father's and attendants' help after the Misbegotten serving the castle rebelled.
Irina asks the Tarnished to deliver a letter persuading her father to leave the castle, but she is murdered before their reunion.
The large sword found by Irina's corpse implies an escaped Misbegotten from Castle Morne was her killer.
Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne, was ordained by Godrick and stays to protect the castle's Grafted Blade Greatsword even as attendants flee the Misbegotten rebellion.
After finding Irina's body, Edgar regrets failing to protect her and swears vengeance on her killers.
Edgar can later be found as an invader at Revengers Shack, and the Shabriri Grape he drops suggests he succumbed to madness from Irina's death.
Hyetta is a blind young woman who resembles Irina and can perceive light by consuming Shabriri Grapes.
Hyetta is initially disgusted that Shabriri Grapes are human eyes but accepts it as necessary to become a finger maiden.
Hyetta mentions other beings with trembling hands and emaciated fingers have also given her Shabriri Grapes.
Completing Hyetta's quest and helping her become a Finger Maiden reveals more information on the Three Fingers and the Frenzied Flame.
Shabriri is a mysterious figure calling himself chaos incarnate, inhabiting the body of Yura, who he claims willingly gave it up.
When met at the Mountaintops of the Giants, Shabriri tries to persuade the Tarnished to become Lord of Frenzied Flame and shares information on the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
Ranni the Witch is the daughter of Rennala and Radagon.
Ranni discovered her own full moon, Ranni's Dark Moon, and learned cold sorceries from the mysterious Snow Witch she encountered in the woods.
Ranni has held Blaidd and Iji dear since childhood.
Ranni defeated the Glintstone Dragon Adula, who then swore allegiance to her.
Blaidd is the half-wolven Shadow of Ranni, granted to her by the Two Fingers when she became an Empyrean.
Blaidd's loyalty lies only with Ranni, whom he considers family, despite being an agent of the Two Fingers.
Even in madness, Blaidd continued to defy his fate and remain faithful to Ranni.
War Counselor Iji is the only friendly Troll the Tarnished encounters, serving as the Carian royal family's blacksmith.
Iji also serves as Ranni's war counselor, providing guidance on the lost city of Nokron.
Iji has watched over Blaidd and Ranni since they were children.
Iji's Mirrorhelm implies he feared the consequences of his treachery against the Greater Will.
Preceptor Seluvis is a magic preceptor serving the Carian Royal family and currently aids Ranni in her search for the dark path.
Seluvis helped Sellen in some way when she was initially exiled from the academy, though Sellen does not seem fond of him.
Seluvis reveals a scheme to betray Ranni and add her, a demigod, to his puppet collection.
It is speculated that Seluvis and Pidia have a connection due to their shared affinity for puppets.
Merchant Kale is one of the nomadic merchants the Tarnished can buy from, acquainted with Blaidd who calls him a busybody.
Kale describes the nomadic clan as spiteful, suggesting their summoning of the frenzied flame was an act of spite.
Witch-Hunter Jerren was originally a nomadic wanderer who became a guest of the Carian royal family, befriending Ranni, Iji, and Radahn.
Jerren promised Ranni and Iji he would slay the Graven Witch Sellen, a longstanding enemy of the Carian family who had committed atrocities against fellow sorcerers.
Jerren wields the Flamberge, a symbol of Redmane Castle, and heralds the beginning of the war festival when first met.
Sorceress Sellen was one of the most promising sorcerers in the history of Raya Lucaria Academy and had a unique glintstone crown.
Sellen was exiled from Raya Lucaria Academy for her obsession with the forbidden primeval current.
Master Lusat and Master Azur were other primeval sorcerers banished from the Academy, and both had their minds broken by glimpsing the primeval current.
According to Jerren, Sellen has killed many fellow sorcerers in her studies.
Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins by the Academy and the Carian Royal Family due to her forbidden pursuits.
The Tarnished can help Sellen transplant her primeval glintstone, essentially her soul, into another compatible body to free her.
Thops is a glintstone sorcerer from Raya Lucaria Academy nicknamed 'Thops the Bluntstone' for lacking talent for powerful sorceries.
If aided, Thops completes his lifelong project, creating Thops's Barrier, a defensive glintstone sorcery that deflects sorceries and incantations back at the caster.
Miriel, Pastor of Vows is a large turtle and steward of the Church of Vows who teaches Absolution though he does not require it himself.
Miriel is well-versed in the history of Rennala and Radagon's union and teaches the Tarnished sorceries and incantations.
Unlike Corhyn, who deems non-Golden Order incantations heresy, Miriel is open-minded toward all sorcery and incantation scrolls given to him.
Albus is a first-generation Albinauric; first-generation Albinaurics were created with defective legs that prevented walking, and when their legs fade, their life fades too.
The Tarnished finds Albus disguised as a pot to escape Gideon's subordinates attacking the Village of the Albinaurics.
Latenna is a first-generation Albinauric and one of many wolf-riding Albinauric archers.
Latenna was interrogated by an agent of Sir Gideon Ofnir, or possibly Gideon himself, about the second half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, leading to the death of her wolf Lobo.
If approached with the right half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, Latenna asks the Tarnished to take her to Apostate Derelict in exchange for revealing the location of the left half.
At Apostate Derelict, Latenna transfers a birthing droplet to a large Albinauric named Phillia, said to be connected to creating new life for the Albinaurics.
Ensha of the Royal Remains is Sir Gideon Ofnir's silent right-hand man.
Ensha's armor, the Royal Remains Set, and his weapon, the Clinging Bone, suggest he is the reanimated remains of a king known as the Soulless King.

It is speculated from Gideon's dialogue that Ensha was tasked with finding both halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion and attacks the Tarnished at the Roundtable Hold to take whichever half they have found.
Tanith is consort to Lord Rykard and the adoptive mother of Rya.
Tanith worked as a dancer in a foreign land until she caught Lord Rykard's eye and became his consort.

Tanith stayed by Rykard's side even after he swore himself to blasphemy and merged with the God-Devouring Serpent, even when his men turned against him and even when she was offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness as an escape.
Bernahl is an Ash of War teacher the Tarnished can first meet in Stormhill.
Bernahl was said to be a Tarnished worthy of becoming Elden Lord, following his destined path without doubt, until his maiden threw herself into 'the fire'.
The Tarnished can later find Bernahl as a recusant at Volcano Manor.
After Rykard is defeated, Bernahl denounces the Greater Will and vows to fell them on behalf of his brother.
Rya's real name is Zorayas, and she is a Man-Serpent disguised as a human working as the scout for Volcano Manor.
Only the Tarnished and Rya's adoptive mother Tanith know of Rya's true serpent form.
Tanith told Rya that she was born by the grace of a great king, but Rya later becomes suspicious of Volcano Manor's secrets and confronts Tanith.
A talisman left behind at the end of Rya's questline suggests her true mother was Daedicar, a woman said to have birthed multiple grotesque children through countless acts of adultery.
Patches the Untethered is a bandit who tricks unsuspecting people into death traps and entrapment schemes.
If spared, Patches sells the Tarnished various goods presumably looted from the corpses of those he successfully tricked.
Patches mentions his band of bandits is made up of foot soldiers and survivors of defeated armies left to fend for themselves.
Patches has taken a liking to Tanith and risks himself to obtain the Dancer's Castanets, hoping to restore her mind after Rykard's defeat.
Diallos is the youngest son of House Hoslow and lives in the shadow of his elder brother, Juno Hoslow.
Unlike Juno, a formidable fighter, Diallos is timid, which does not fit his family's bloodshed-focused motto.
Despite their differences, Diallos and Juno care deeply for each other, with Juno doting on Diallos and Diallos looking up to him.
Diallos hopes to become a champion like his brother but grows disillusioned and seeks a different purpose.
Jar-Bairn is a young jar living in Jarburg, a secret village of peaceful Living Jars.
Jar-Bairn is one of the few Living Jars capable of speaking to the Tarnished and is a warrior jar like his uncle Alexander.
Jar-Bairn can be found talking in his sleep about reuniting with Alexander, poachers destroying the Living Pots at Jarburg, or Diallos taking care of him.
Iron Fist Alexander is an older Living Jar who left Jarburg to seek great battle and hone his skills.
Warrior jars like Alexander are Living Jars filled with the remains of warriors, destined to leave home and journey alone to become great champions.
Blackguard Big Boggart is a Tarnished and former criminal selling boiled prawns and crabs, first at the Boilprawn Shack and later outside the royal capital.
Boggart may have previously been convicted of thievery, having stolen Rya's necklace.
Boggart used to be cellmates with Dung Eater, witnessing him defile a friend's body with the Seedbed Curse, the most harrowing experience of Boggart's life.
Dung Eater is a Tarnished who bears the heart of an Omen, as suggested by his armor.
Even before returning to the Lands Between, Dung Eater was a merciless killer who defiled his victims' corpses with Seedbed Curses, cursing their souls to never return to the Erdtree.
Enia is a Finger Reader Crone the Tarnished encounters at the Roundtable Hold, interpreting the wisdom of the Greater Will through the Two Fingers.
Unlike other finger readers who become frantic after losing their Two Fingers, Enia remains calm.
Despite being an agent of the Greater Will, Enia supports the Tarnished burning down the Erdtree once her Two Fingers stop communicating with her.
Enia claims that before the Tarnished, another person had gathered two Great Runes.
Radagon is characterized by flowing red hair and is Queen Marika's second chosen consort and a great warrior.
Radagon reportedly hated the red tint of his hair.
A statue in the Royal Capital reveals that Marika and Radagon are one and the same being.
Despite being shunned, Morgott still loved the Golden Order.
Miquella's connection to St. Trina, revealed in the DLC, shows they are two manifestations of the same being, echoing the duality of Radagon and Marika.

Key NPCs met in the Realm of Shadow include Needle Knight Leda, a loyal follower of Miquella; Redmane Freyja, a former Radahn warrior; a Hornsent representative; and Sir Ansbach, a former servant of Mohg.
St. Trina, an enigmatic figure barely mentioned in the base game, is explored further through interactions with her and her follower Thiollier, revealing her connection to Miquella.
Ansbach was once part of the Pureblood Knights, though the crest on his armor has nearly faded over time.
Despite knowing his loyalty to Mohg is neither logical nor just, Ansbach still holds onto his oath, reflecting an inner struggle.
Freyja reflects on the complexity of potentially fighting alongside or against former allies like Sir Ansbach.
Hornsent holds a deep grudge against the Erdtree, viewing it as an enemy of his people.
Hornsent views Marika as a betrayer of his people.
Despite his hatred, Hornsent follows an oath to Miquella and offers assistance to the player.
Hornsent provides maps marking crosses tied to his people's suffering as the player aligns with Miquella.
Hornsent refuses to accept alms or gifts out of pride, but rewards the player with maps and guidance if aided.
After Messmer's death, Hornsent expresses satisfaction but states his thirst for vengeance extends to Marika and the entire Erdtree.
Igon is a broken drake warrior consumed by pain and a burning need for revenge against the dread dragon Bayle.
Igon once sought honor through Dragon Communion, shown by the design of his armor pieces.
Igon's soul clings to the mountain where his battle with Bayle took place, and he asks the player to climb the peak to face the dragon.
When the player defeats the Jagged Peak Drake, Igon reflects on the warrior he once was before asking the player to continue his fight against Bayle.
The Dragon Communion Priestess compares Igon's ambition and hunger to Bayle's fiery spirit and relentless drive.
After Bayle is defeated, Igon's spirit is freed and finally able to rest, his revenge realized.
Moore is a gentle giant, a follower of Miquella, and a member of the Forager Brood, a group dedicated to finding crafting materials and recipes across the Land of Shadow.
When the Great Rune breaks, Moore is visibly affected but continues clinging to his devotion to Miquella.
Moore provides Thiollier with Black Syrup after being asked to find it.
If a member of the forager brood is killed or harmed, Moore reacts with grief and anger, calling it an unforgivable tragedy.
After the final boss is defeated, Moore laments the loss of his brood and the absence of allies including Lady Leda, Father Dane, Sir Ansbach, Freyja, Thiollier, and the Hornsent.
Needle Knight Leda is the leader of Miquella's band of followers in the Realm of Shadow.
Leda references Dane, a silent monk who has served Miquella longer than she has, describing him as reserved but a formidable warrior.
After the Great Rune breaks, Leda grows suspicious of her fellow followers and proposes eliminating the Hornsent, fearing his vengeance could threaten Miquella's cause.
Leda identifies Sir Ansbach, a former commander of the Pureblood Knights, as a potential danger due to his past involvement with Miquella's blood blade.
After defeating Sir Ansbach, Leda reflects on the weight of her actions but accepts them as the price for ensuring Miquella's continued favor.
Thiollier is a non-combatant Tarnished character skilled in crafting poison rather than fighting, found at the Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace.
Thiollier serves Miquella and mentions Lady Leda when first met, acknowledging shared devotion to the same deity.
After the Great Rune breaks, Thiollier becomes haunted by memories of St. Trina, the goddess of slumber, and longs for her poison to grant him eternal sleep.
Thiollier travels to find St. Trina's resting place in the southern part of the world, becoming increasingly obsessive and erratic.
Thiollier eventually becomes hostile, accusing the player of lying if they try to speak for St. Trina, leading to a final confrontation.
Hornsent Grandam belongs to the ancient Hornsent race that once thrived in Belurat Tower Settlement and was connected to the Divine Beast Dancing Lion.
Hornsent Grandam greets the Tarnished with suspicion, accusing them of complicity in Messmer's atrocities.
Dryleaf Dane is a master of unarmed martial combat, a devoted follower of Miquella, and a sworn ally of Leda.
Count Ymir is the High Priest of Manus Metyr Cathedral and a vendor for glintstone sorceries.
Count Ymir shares philosophical musings about the Greater Will, the Erdtree, and the world's flaws.
Count Ymir's companion Jolán can be summoned during specific encounters once her questline advances.
The Dragon Communion Priestess is a surviving Ancient Dragon and worshipper of Dragonlord Placidusax.
Jolán is a loyal warrior serving Count Ymir, found standing on a pillar beside him in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr.
Jolán warns the player that crossing Count Ymir will bring regret, though she shows respect if the player earns his trust.
Jolán calls Count Ymir a guiding star in the dark sky and believes him to be the only true light in the night.
If the player betrays or harms Count Ymir, Jolán will fight to protect his will.
Fire Knight Queelign is a knight loyal to Queen Marika, introduced in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.
Fire Knight Queelign is first encountered as an NPC invader in Belurat Tower Settlement and the Church of Crusade.
The Fire Giants lived at the Mountaintops of the Giants, a frozen region at the world's highest point.
The Land of Shadow is a dark realm obscured by the Erdtree where the goddess Marika first set foot.
Leyndell is built around the Erdtree's massive golden roots, which arch through the city like exposed bones.
Leyndell has been sealed off from normal time, its remaining soldiers and knights still loyal to an order that no longer functions since the Shattering.
The Lake of Rot will kill a person almost instantly if they remain immersed in it for more than a few moments.
Patches' Emporium can be accessed upon reaching Volcano Manor.

The Realm of Shadow is divided into ten distinct areas: Gravesite Plain, Scadu Altus, Rauh Base, Ancient Ruins of Rauh, Cerulean Coast, Charo's Hidden Grave, Jagged Peak, Abyssal Woods, Finger Ruins of Rhia, and Scaduview.
The Hornsent character is found with Freyja at the Three-Path Cross in Gravesite Plain.
Moore can first be encountered at the Main Gate Cross Site of Grace near Belurat Tower Settlement, accompanied by Sir Ansbach.
Leda is found at the Highroad Cross Site of Grace near Hornsent.
St. Trina is located in the deepest part of Stone Coffin Fissure, within the Garden of Deep Purple.
The Elden Beast's essence became the Elden Ring, a cosmic entity that was never forged but existed as a living expression of cosmic law.
Hoarah Loux took on the golden lion spirit Serosh, the Beast Regent, which lived on his shoulders and suppressed his violent nature, allowing him to become Godfrey, the first Elden Lord.
Marika removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and sealed it inside her shadowbound beast, Maliketh.
As tradition dictates, Rennala bestowed a Moon Greatsword upon her spouse Radagon.
After returning to Marika, Radagon reforged his Moon Greatsword into the Golden Order Greatsword.
Miquella gave Malenia a needle made of unalloyed gold that suppressed her Scarlet Rot, though he could not cure it.
The Finger-Slayer Blade was forged specifically to kill the Fingers, the cosmic emissaries of the Greater Will.
When summoned, Melina wields the Blade of Calling, a dagger previously owned by a kindling maiden.
Blaidd's sword, the Royal Greatsword, was imbued with cold magic as proof of his loyalty to Ranni.
According to Jerren, the blades smithed by Iji were blunt but resistant to decay from scarlet rot.
The Graven-School Talisman notes that fashioning sorcerers' bodies into 'seeds of stars' is one method of pursuing the primeval current, suggesting the practice requires human sacrifice.
Albus safeguards the right half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, said to be key to reaching Miquella's Haligtree, the Albinaurics' promised land.
Living Jar Shards contain traces of magical power and fetch high prices, making Living Jars a target for poachers.
The Ironjar Aromatic is a forbidden defense-boosting consumable made from Living Jar Shards by Depraved Perfumers.
The Glintstone Kris symbolizes the unity between the Capital of Leyndell and the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Mohg used his weapon, Mohgwyn's Sacred Spear, to further communicate with the Formless Mother.
The Blasphemous Claw, a gift from his sister Ranni, allows Rykard to challenge Maliketh as a last resort.
Throughout the Land of Shadow, players find crosses symbolizing pieces of Miquella's being that he sheds in preparation for rebirth.
Ansbach's attire slightly boosts abilities related to blood magic and dynastic skills.
Freyja's armor bears a black woolen mantle and golden markings symbolizing her past rank in Radahn's forces.
Freyja carries the Golden Lion Shield, a symbol awarded to only the most valorous knights of Radahn's personal guard.
Igon's armor set, Igon's Set, is mismatched and tattered, reflecting his past as a battlefield scavenger.
Igon's Furled Finger is a gnarled, discolored finger item that can be used to summon Igon to battle.
Thiollier warns the player not to follow his example, as St. Trina's poison would plunge them into eternal slumber.
Dryleaf Dane leaves a Monk's Missive inviting challengers to test their worth against him in the eastern lands.
Count Ymir gifts the player the Hole-Laden Necklace and a Ruins Map early in his questline.
Queelign's spirit can be summoned using the Fire Knight Queelign item, an ashen remains, causing him to attack immediately with his fiery greatsword.
St. Trina was referenced in the base game through item descriptions such as St. Trina's Torch, hinting at her connection to Miquella.
In battle, Ansbach uses the Furious Blade of Ansbach, an incantation summoning a bloodflame blade that he lunges with to strike enemies, becoming stronger when charged.
Ansbach also wields the Obsidian Lamina, a slender scythe relying on skill rather than tricks.

Freyja wields a Greatsword decorated with a mane, symbolizing her connection to Radahn and her strength as a warrior, and carries the Golden Lion Shield, a symbol of Radahn's personal guard awarded to only his most valorous knights.
Igon created his own weapon, Igon's Harpoon, a great arrow adorned with sharp gravel stone pieces designed to be deadly against dragons.
Igon's Greatbow is crafted from dragon bones bound with rope and scarred by claws, enhancing the power of his harpoons.
Queelign's Greatsword was remade by Queelign in the shape of the lance once wielded by his liege, symbolizing his desire to become a second Impaler.

Dragon Lord Placidusax is a multi-headed ancient dragon who once served as an Elden Lord of a previous age under a god that vanished when the Greater Will arrived; he is found in a pocket of stopped time within crumbling Farum Azula, waiting eternally for a god that will never return.
Because the death curse mark was split, Godwyn's soul died but his body remained alive, corrupting and spreading underground as a growth known as the Prince of Death.
Godrick the Grafted retreated to Stormveil Castle after inheriting his Great Rune and began grafting the limbs of conquered enemies onto his own body.

Morgott, the Omen King, took his lineage's Great Rune to Leyndell and placed himself on the Elden Throne as a guardian rather than as Elden Lord, disguising himself as the merchant and prophet Margit to warn tarnished away from the capital.
Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, took his Great Rune to Volcano Manor and merged with a great serpent, becoming a god-devouring blasphemy.

Radahn, the Starscourge, claimed his Great Rune and continued holding the stars in place using gravity magic, but survived a later battle only for the scarlet rot to consume his mind, reducing him to a feral, mindless creature that ate corpses.

After Godwyn the Golden was murdered on the Night of the Black Knives, Fortissax descended underground to fight the spreading death blight and protect Godwyn's remains, a battle it still fights eternally and has never won.
When fought in the ruined desert north of Redmane Castle, Radahn still rides Leonard even while feral and consumed by rot, and Leonard stays beside Radahn's body after his death.

Malenia wakes only when the tarnished disturbs her after navigating the Consecrated Snowfield and the corrupted Haligtree; upon waking she says, "I dreamt for so long. My flesh was dull gold and my blood was rot," and "I await him still," referring to Miquella.
Malenia introduces herself as Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and declares she has never known defeat.
Inside the Erdtree, the Tarnished confronts Radagon, described as Marika's other, devoted half who tried to repair what Marika broke.

When Radagon falls in battle, he transforms into Marika and then into the Elden Beast, the living embodiment of the Greater Will's Order, fought as a creature of golden starlight within a void of absolute darkness.
Marika and Radagon are revealed to be the same divine being sharing one body, a twist revealed through the penultimate boss encounter of the game.
Near the end of the game, Hoarah Loux tears the spirit Serosh from his shoulders, killing his restrainer and becoming his unrestrained primal self again mid-battle.
Mohg built Mohgwyn Palace around a wound in the world tied to the Formless Mother and declared himself Lord of Blood.
After Melina's sacrifice, the base game does not fully resolve what happens to her, leaving it ambiguous whether she is gone or transformed.
If the Tarnished has accepted the Frenzied Flame, Melina does not sacrifice herself and instead becomes a figure sworn to deliver the Tarnished's destined death.
After the Elden Beast falls, the Elden Ring lies shattered and Marika appears fractured and silent, awaiting the Tarnished's choice of ending.
Nepheli's questline resolves with her ruling a restored Limgrave from its throne, presented as one of the game's unambiguously positive outcomes.
The Age of Fracture ending has the Tarnished mend the Elden Ring without additional power or intention, becoming Elden Lord while the Golden Order and Greater Will's structure continue as before.
The Age of Order ending requires completing the questlines of Brother Corhyn and Goldmask.
Goldmask's mending rune creates a transcendental Golden Order meant to rise above the corruption of individual divine personalities.
The Age of Duskyn ending comes from completing the questline of Fia, the Deathbed Companion, who holds Tarnished in her embrace to share in their life force.
Fia's mending rune restores natural death to the world, allowing those who live in death to finally rest and ending the Erdtree's cycle of capturing and recycling souls.
The Blessing of Despair ending comes from the Dung Eater's questline.
The Blessing of Despair ending is considered the darkest of the Elden Lord endings, reflecting a nihilistic worldview given power over reality.
The Lord of the Frenzied Flame ending requires descending beneath Leyndell's sewers to find the Three Fingers and allow them to grant the Frenzied Flame.
Accepting the Frenzied Flame locks the Tarnished into becoming the Lord of Chaos, the instrument of the Frenzied Flame's apocalyptic vision to burn the Erdtree and everything else to ash.
In the Frenzied Flame ending, Melina watches the destruction and vows to deliver the Tarnished's destined death.
The Age of Stars ending belongs to Ranni and requires completing her questline, becoming her champion and lord, and retrieving her ring.
In the Age of Stars ending, after the Elden Beast falls, Ranni's summon sign appears offering the Tarnished a choice instead of Marika's fractured form.
When summoned, Ranni appears in her true form as an enormous, radiant, divine being who replaces Marika in the world's structure, with the Dark Moon becoming the new guiding light.
Ranni tells the Tarnished she will give birth to a new and fleeting world and calls the Tarnished her consort, and together they leave the Lands Between on a thousand-year voyage into the stars.
In the Age of Stars ending, the world below begins its first night without the golden light that has governed it since before living memory.
Ranni describes her intended Age of Stars as one of unalloyed cold darkness, a thousand-year voyage into darkness guided by the Dark Moon.
In Ranni's envisioned age, the Erdtree would no longer be the center of power, the golden economy of souls would be disrupted, and mortal natural death would be restored in some form.
Whether Ranni's Age of Stars ending is truly good for the people of the Lands Between is left ambiguous by the game.
St. Trina urges the player to kill Miquella to grant him forgiveness for the tragedy his divinity would bring.
Under the Golden Order, ordinary people did not truly die; their spirits returned to the Erdtree through underground catacombs to be sustained or sent back.
Demigods and lords under the Golden Order could be killed in battle but could not permanently die, due to the removal of the Rune of Death.
The Tarnished receives a call in the form of a golden guiding thread of grace that leads toward the Erdtree, promising the chance to restore the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord.
Grace can call to Tarnished descendants generations later even if they have no direct memory of the original promise, drawing them back to the Lands Between.
Crucible-referencing incantations let the caster temporarily manifest animalistic traits such as tails, wings, or armored carapaces, echoing the primordial blending of life.
Tarnished who die can be revived repeatedly by the grace that resurrects them, allowing effectively unlimited deaths and returns.
The game describes the power of the Great Runes as a 'mad taint' rather than a pure gift, amplifying each demigod's existing traits.
The grace light from the Erdtree now appears only as thin, faint Sites of Grace guiding tarnished, remnants of a nearly depleted divine power.
Malenia heals herself by draining the player's vitality with each successful attack.
Malenia can bloom a smaller version of the Scarlet Aeonia during battle, filling the arena with rot.
The Tarnished consumes Great Runes taken from fallen demigods over the course of the journey.
The Sites of Grace are depicted narratively as fragments of the Erdtree's fading grace and the world's memory of what it was meant to be.
Each Site of Grace points in a direction suggesting where the player should go next, but players can choose to ignore this guidance and explore elsewhere.
It is implied that warrior jars absorb the essence and martial prowess of the fallen warriors they consume.
Before being granted an audience with Rykard and joining the family, newly recruited Tarnished must invade fellow Tarnished to prove their resolve.
Leda urges the player to touch the withered arm, a portal to the Realm of Shadow where Miquella resides.
Dryleaf Dane's fighting style, Dane's Footwork, emphasizes powerful and precise kicks developed through training under a waterfall.
Elden Ring sold over 25 million copies.
The mythology of Elden Ring was created by George R. R. Martin, while the narrative and worldbuilding were developed by Hidetaka Miyazaki and FromSoftware.

In cut content, Kale would have discovered his people, the Great Caravan, were falsely accused of worshipping the Three Fingers and summoning the frenzied flame, filling him with spite toward the Greater Will and Golden Order.
FromSoftware has stated that Elden Ring is an independent title with its own storyline, though some fans theorize it may connect to the Dark Souls series as a prequel.
Hewg the Blacksmith was assigned by Queen Marika to forge a weapon capable of slaying God but was unable to complete it in time, as stated in his dialogue.
Some of the most important discoveries in the Lands Between, such as underground cities, hidden questlines, and optional bosses, are not indicated by the Sites of Grace guidance.

Fan theories propose that the puppets found in the hidden basement behind Caria Manor, including a Nox, an Omenkiller, Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, Finger Maiden Therolina, a Jarwright, and a hidden Sellen puppet, may all belong to Seluvis.
Theories suggest the Omenkiller puppet may have been meant to frame Gideon Ofnir for the slaughter in the Albinauric village, disillusioning Nephali.
In truth, Miquella orchestrated his own kidnapping, having charmed Mohg to gain access to the Realm of Shadow through Mohg's blood rituals.
Nokron the Eternal City is theorized to have succeeded in creating the god-slaying weapon Marika sought, but was accused of treason and destroyed, its remnants banished underground.

It is implied Marika came to understand that the Greater Will was indifferent rather than benevolent, and that the Golden Order's gift of immortality was actually a means of recycling souls to feed the Erdtree, a system that also feeds the Greater Will's cosmic design.

Marika began to harbor doubts about the Greater Will and the Golden Order, and is speculated to have had a hand in the Night of the Black Knives due to rumored connections with the Black Knife Assassins.
Rykard had a hand in the Night of the Black Knives, though to an unclear extent.

One theory holds that Marika did not shatter the Elden Ring purely out of rage over Godwyn's death, but that his death partially restored her sanity enough to break the Ring in an attempt to find the strongest champion to become Elden Lord or free her from suffering.
A theory suggests Marika created Melina and gave her the mission to burn down the Erdtree, and Melina wandered the Lands Between searching for her purpose.
The theory continues that the resulting war of the demigods ended without a clear winner, as Radahn and Malenia proved equal in strength.

The theory further suggests Marika used her last shimmer of grace to invite even Tarnished to compete for the Great Runes and become Elden Lord, granting them revival upon death, while Radagon tries to hinder this plan using the Erdtree's roots.
Ranni sought to follow the Dark Moon, a distant cosmic force offering freedom rather than order, instead of the Erdtree's Golden Order.
The Greater Will is not the only cosmic power in Elden Ring's theology; it dominates the current age through the Erdtree and Marika's godhood while other Outer Gods contest for influence.
If the Scarlet Aeonia blooms three times, Malenia will become a true goddess and complete vessel for the rot; she has bloomed once so far.
Frenzied Flame theology holds that the Greater Will erred by creating individuals, and that all suffering should be melted back into unified oneness.
Fia has devoted herself to restoring natural death in a world that forcibly removes it, loving the Prince of Death despite its inability to love her back.
The Lands Between is not a world waiting to be saved but one already broken in ways a single Tarnished cannot simply fix by fighting to the top.
Many demigods the Tarnished fights became monstrous not from birth but because the world, their great runes, or prolonged grief shaped them that way.
Melina is characterized as the first genuinely kind presence the Tarnished encounters in the Lands Between.
All six Elden Ring endings involve continuing something—a cycle, a new order, a destruction, or a departure—rather than providing a clean, final resolution.
Elden Ring's narrative explores themes of inherited systems and structures that claim authority based on an origin story the player never witnessed.
The Erdtree is characterized as a parasitic structure whose golden light hides the fact that the Greater Will is distant and alien.
None of the alternative powers challenging the Golden Order—Ranni's cold moon, Miquella's compassion, Goldmask's order, or the Frenzied Flame's destruction—are presented as clearly better solutions.
Some theorize Bernahl's maiden succumbed to the frenzied flame, while others theorize she was thrown into the Forge of the Giants as fuel to burn the Erdtree, similar to Melina.

It is speculated that the person who gathered two Great Runes before the Tarnished was either Bernahl, whose armor suggests he was worthy of becoming Lord, or Vyke, said to be the closest anyone came to becoming Elden Lord before turning to the Frenzied Flame.
There is speculation Radagon may be a smaller-sized Fire Giant, based on descriptions of the Sword of Milos and Giant's Red Braid.
Another theory holds that Radagon was cursed with red hair by the Fire Giants as a result of the Golden Order's war against them.
It is speculated that Golden Order Incantations require both Faith and Intelligence because Radagon learned sorceries as Rennala's consort and incantations as Marika's consort.
It is unclear whether Marika and Radagon were always one being, whether Radagon is a fragment of Marika, or whether they became one after becoming consorts, as Melina's dialogue suggests.
Community lore theories debate whether the Lands Between's timeline is linear or cyclical, with multiple Erdtrees possibly rising after prior ages ruled by Giants, Dragons, or Tarnished.
One theory suggests the Elden Ring might be a symbolic measure of power, an artifact controlled by the Elden Lord, or a form assumed by the Elden Beast to fulfill the Greater Will's goals.
One theory suggests Marika shattered the Elden Ring to drive Godfrey out of the Lands Between and initiate the Long March of the Tarnished.

Fan theories debate whether Marika is a fixed entity vested with godhood by the Greater Will, or a specific being who arrived from the lands of the Numen in a manner similar to the Tarnished's recall.
Some theorize that Radagon and Marika's relationship mirrors the duality of Miquella and St. Trina, both being two aspects of one being.
Fan theory suggests the Erdtree may simply be the Greater Will's method of diverting the souls of the dead to harvest life-force and dominate death itself through the Golden Order.
