A community theory suggests the Nox may have initiated the Night of the Black Knives as a plot possibly connected to Ranni, though her exact role (mastermind or ritual performer) is debated.
Count Ymir reveals disillusionment with the Erdtree and Marika, lamenting the world's inherent flaws and humanity's inability to find redemption.
St. Trina expresses concern that Miquella's ascension to godhood would be a curse rather than a blessing, trapping him beyond saving.

events.summary: In the primordial Crucible age, all life existed in chaotic communion without species or hierarchy, centered around an older Great Tree, and ancient dragons may have followed their own prior cosmic order.
Dragon Lord Placidusax once served as Elden Lord of that earlier age under a god that vanished when the Greater Will arrived, and now waits eternally in stopped time.

The Greater Will sent its daughter Marika, a Numen from outside the Lands Between chosen as an Empyrean, along with the golden Elden Beast, into the Lands Between; Marika became a god at the Gate of Divinity, and the Elden Beast's essence became the Elden Ring.

Marika constructed the Golden Order and chose the fierce warrior chieftain Hoarah Loux as her consort; he took on the beast-spirit Serosh to quell his bloodlust and became Godfrey, the first Elden Lord.

The new Erdtree grew around the Elden Ring, subsuming the old Great Tree, and through countless wars became the embodiment of order; former Crucible-blessed beings such as Omens and Misbegotten were reclassified as cursed and enslaved, while the Nox rebelled and were exiled underground.
Marika removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and entrusted it to her Shadow, Maliketh, to lock away, ensuring demigods and mortals under the Golden Order could not permanently die.

Under Marika's direction, Godfrey and the Golden Order waged wars of conquest: against the Storm Lord, the Fire Giants and their Fell God, the serpent god of Mt. Gelmir, and the Carian sorcerers of Raya Lucaria, with uncertain instigation in the wars against the Dragons and the Gloam-Eyed Queen's Godskin Apostles.

The Fire Giant war nearly annihilated the giants; one was spared and cursed to guard the Forge of the Giants' flame of ruin forever, while the Fell God survived diminished in the Mountaintops of the Giants.

Rennala's mastery of lunar sorcery made her head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and matriarch of the Carian royal family; Radagon married her, ending the Academy-Erdtree conflict, but this marriage was later dissolved when Marika recalled him.

With no enemies left to fight, Godfrey's purposeless spirit led Marika to strip him and his warriors of grace, exiling them across the Sea of Fog to the Badlands as the first Tarnished, promising eventual return of their grace to become Elden Lord.

Marika took Godfrey's twin sons by their union, Morgott and Mohg, born with Omen traits, and had them hidden away in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath Leyndell, while Godwyn the Golden grew to be her beloved firstborn and bonded with the dragon Fortissax.

Gladiatorial combat as Erdtree ritual was common under Godfrey's reign, ending when Radagon became Marika's new consort; Radagon led wars including the campaign against Liurnia, eventually meeting and marrying Rennala after the Liurnian Wars.

Radagon and Rennala had three children: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni; but when Marika recalled Radagon to rejoin her, he gifted Rennala an amber egg and departed, devastating her and causing the Academy's scholars to rebel and imprison her.

Marika and Radagon (one being) also had twins Miquella and Malenia, both cursed from birth—Miquella with eternal childhood, Malenia with Scarlet Rot—and Messmer, cursed with an inner Abyssal Serpent, was sent to purge the Hornsent people of the Realm of Shadow.

Elsewhere, exiled heretics such as Kale's Great Caravan summoned the flame of frenzy underground, and Shabriri's punishment for slander is remembered as the first outbreak of the maddening Frenzied Flame sickness.
Rykard met and took as consort the dancer Tanith, while later, disillusioned with the Order's rule by force, he would seek forbidden power.

Ranni, groomed as an Empyrean candidate of the Two Fingers, rejected her fated destiny; one night while stargazing with her mother Rennala she discovered her own Dark Moon and began learning forbidden lunar sorcery from the Snow Witch Renna.

On a night of wintry fog, Ranni masterminded the Night of the Black Knives, stealing a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and using Black Knife Assassins to kill Godwyn the Golden and many of Marika's other kin, marking the deaths of the first demigod.

Because Ranni took her own life at the same moment, the death curse mark split in two instead of completing, leaving Godwyn's body alive but soulless while his soul died, and Ranni's soul survived by design, transferred into a doll body modeled after Renna.

Godwyn's soulless body festered beneath Leyndell's roots, becoming known as the Prince of Death, an entity tied to the new category of undying 'those who live in death,' hunted by the Golden Order and later cared for by sympathizers like Fia.

Marika, devastated by Godwyn's death—the most grievous loss among her murdered kin—shattered the Elden Ring in a final act of rebellion against the Greater Will, an act theorized to reflect her disillusionment with the Order's true nature; Radagon, sharing her body but a different will, tried to repair it.
The shards of the shattered Ring became Great Runes claimed by Marika's demigod children, whose corrupting madness ignited the Shattering, a war between the demigods that fractured the unified realm.

Godrick retreated to Stormveil grafting conquered limbs onto himself; Morgott took the throne of Leyndell as a hidden guardian disguised as Margit; Rykard fused with the God-Devouring Serpent at Volcano Manor for immortality, alienating most followers except Tanith; Mohg escaped confinement to found his own dynasty.
Radahn halted the stars with gravity magic to prevent Ranni's foretold Age of Stars, then marched to war against Malenia, whose Haligtree army fought his forces in the bloody Battle of Aeonia.

Malenia and Radahn fought to a draw as evenly matched champions; her needle broke, unleashing the Scarlet Aeonia that transformed Caelid into a rotted wasteland, after which she fell into a deep coma and was carried back to the Haligtree by the knight Finlay.

Meanwhile Miquella grew the Haligtree from a sapling using his own blood, envisioning a sanctuary free of the Golden Order's discrimination, though scarlet rot still corrupted it even as Malenia slept awaiting his return.

During the Shattering's chaos, Mohg kidnapped the sleeping Miquella from the Haligtree, secretly at Miquella's own manipulation, wrapping him in a golden cocoon and feeding him blood in a ritual to elevate him to divine status via the Formless Mother's power.

Other conflicts of the Shattering era included Gowry's devotion to Malenia's cause after Aeonia's bloom, Jerren joining Radahn's army instead of fulfilling his vow against Sellen, and the Golden Order's Second Defense of Leyndell led by Morgott.

With no victor and the Greater Will's guidance seemingly withdrawn, the Shattering ended in stalemate, the demigods retreating to their fractured domains, and doubt began spreading among Golden Order faithful about the Order's infallibility.

Amid the long stalemate, figures such as Vyke sacrificed himself into Frenzied Flame madness trying to save his finger maiden, and Hewg the misbegotten blacksmith labored in vain on a god-slaying weapon commissioned by Marika.

Eventually the Radahn Festival was held, inviting warriors worldwide to grant the feral, rot-consumed General Radahn an honorable death; when he fell, a falling star shattered the earth and opened the buried city of Nokron.

This opening of Nokron was exactly what Ranni needed to continue her plan: to retrieve the Finger-Slayer Blade from Nokron and later claim the Dark Moon Ring at the Moonlight Altar, meant for the consort who would help her usurp the Two Fingers and Greater Will.

Generations later, the call of grace summons a new wave of Tarnished, including the game's protagonist, back to the Lands Between to compete for the shattered Great Runes and the throne of Elden Lord.

The Tarnished's journey passes through Limgrave and Stormveil Castle, encountering Morgott (as Margit), Godrick the Grafted's grotesque grafting experiments, and local figures like Kenneth Haight, Nepheli Loux, Gostoc, Roderika, Boc, Irina, and Edgar of Castle Morne, whose personal tragedies unfold along the way.

The Tarnished travels through Liurnia and the Academy, aiding Rennala (still clutching Radagon's amber egg), Ranni's retinue (Blaidd, Iji, Seluvis), and the exiled sorcerers Sellen and Thops, eventually helping free Ranni's soul-doll body and becoming her consort candidate.

In Caelid and the Haligtree, the Tarnished encounters Malenia's daughter Millicent, raised by Gowry to inherit the scarlet rot legacy, before waking Malenia herself deep within Elphael, who awaits Miquella's return.

At Volcano Manor, the Tarnished encounters Rykard's recusant faction—Tanith, Rya (secretly the serpent Zorayas), Bernahl, and Patches—rebels against the Greater Will who ultimately aid in Rykard's downfall.

Elsewhere the Tarnished meets Mohg's Mohgwyn Dynasty followers including White Mask Varre and the Bloody Fingers, hunted by Yura, as well as the Dung Eater's atrocities and Fia's compassionate care for the dead.

The Tarnished also crosses paths with the Round Table Hold's Golden Order scholars Corhyn, Goldmask, and Enia, who begin questioning the Order's flaws, and with Frenzied Flame agents like Hyetta and Shabriri offering the path of apocalypse.

Continuing north, the Tarnished aids Albinauric survivors Albus and Latenna against Gideon Ofnir's schemes, and battles Fortissax, who still eternally fights the death blight beneath the earth to protect Godwyn's remains.

At Mountaintops of the Giants, the Tarnished learns Melina's true purpose was always to sacrifice herself as kindling to burn open the Erdtree, a role possibly designed by Marika herself, and she carries this out at the Forge of the Giants.

Entering the burned-open Erdtree, the Tarnished confronts Radagon, Marika's devoted other half who tried to mend what she broke, learns the truth that Marika and Radagon are one being, and battles Hoarah Loux's unleashed primal spirit before Radagon transforms into Marika and then the Elden Beast itself.
With the Elden Beast defeated, the shattered Elden Ring and fractured Marika await the Tarnished's final choice, which will determine the fate of the Lands Between.

Possible endings include mending the Ring simply as new Elden Lord (Age of Fracture), Goldmask and Corhyn's transcendental Age of Order, Fia's Age of Duskyn restoring natural death, Dung Eater's nihilistic Blessing of Despair, or submission to the Frenzied Flame as Lord of Chaos, watched by Melina in each case.

Alternatively, by completing Ranni's questline and returning with the Dark Moon Ring, the Tarnished can choose the Age of Stars: Ranni rises as a new divine being replacing Marika, guiding a thousand-year voyage of cold darkness away from the Erdtree's golden order, its ultimate benefit to the world left ambiguous.
Elsewhere, Nepheli Loux's storyline concludes with her ruling a restored Limgrave, portrayed as one of the more hopeful, unambiguous outcomes of the fractured world.

In a separate expanded chapter (Shadow of the Erdtree), Miquella, having orchestrated his own path through Mohg's blood rituals, journeys to the Realm of Shadow to attempt his own ascension to godhood using the same Gate of Divinity and a ritual to capture Radahn's soul into Mohg's body.

In the Realm of Shadow, the Tarnished meets Miquella's scattered followers—Leda, Freyja, Dane, Ansbach, Hornsent, Moore, Thiollier, Count Ymir, Jolán, and Queelign—each shaped by loyalty, grief, or vengeance from the old wars of the Hornsent's persecution by Messmer and Marika.
The dragon-warrior Igon, seeking vengeance against the dread dragon Bayle since their ancient duel, is finally freed from his torment when the Tarnished defeats Bayle atop the Jagged Peak.

When Miquella's Great Rune breaks amid the Tarnished's intervention, his followers fracture in grief and suspicion, revealing his manipulative charm even as his compassion is judged genuine but flawed, and St. Trina's identity as his hidden dual self is finally revealed.
